key_insight: tEHR uses pretrained language semantics to encode longitudinal health records, with clinical descriptions and numerical values contributing to prediction performance.
clinical_relevance: This approach could support EHR-based risk prediction, but the abstract does not establish readiness for clinical use.
method: Represent structured EHR events using natural-language descriptions.
Continue pretraining a causal language model on longitudinal EHR text.
Use LoRA for task-specific discriminative fine-tuning.
evidence_signal: Evaluation covered four MIMIC-IV prediction tasks and CPRD pancreatic cancer prediction at 1–12-month horizons; Mistral-7B-v0.3 achieved the strongest overall performance among the tested tEHR backbones.
watch_item: The abstract provides no numerical performance estimates or prospective clinical evaluation, limiting assessment of clinical utility.
paper_title: Evaluating Pretrained Language Semantics for Structured EHR Prediction Tasks
